# Hand-annotated motive families in Mozart, Piano Sonata in C major K. 545, first movement, the exposition (measures 1-28), for the
# motive analysis (standard-form's motive adapter, run on the soprano: the highest sounding note at each attack).
#
# SOURCE: the Neue Mozart-Ausgabe (IX/25/2) and the IMSLP scan of the first edition. Neither was available when this file was written, so
# the edition is the one to check against.
# STATUS: DRAFT, NOT YET CHECKED AGAINST THE PRINTED SCORE. A hand reading of tests/fixtures/framework-v1-corpus/"Mozart 545.mid" (the top
# line of each measure, dumped by attack with its beat), listing the figures that recur in plain sight: the scale sequence of measures 5-8,
# the repeated gestures of measures 14-17, the descending sequence of measures 18-21, and the octave echo of measures 26-27. It was NOT
# derived from the output of the motive adapter. A human should confirm it against an edition before it is relied on. Motives the reading
# was not sure of (for example in the development-like passages of measures 9-13 and 22-25) are left out; the lack of a family here is not
# an annotation that there is none.
#
# The reading follows standard-form's vocabulary: a motive is a short recurring figure; it recurs EXACTLY, in REAL transposition (the same
# semitone intervals from another pitch) or in TONAL transposition (the same steps of the scale, so other semitones: a diatonic
# sequence). Each family lists the occurrences by measure and beat; the first is the prototype and is "exact".
#
# FORMAT, one per line (lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored):
#   meter <beats per measure> <beat length as a fraction of a whole note>
#   range <first measure> <last measure>
#   family <name>
#   occurrence <measure> <beat> <exact|real|tonal>     of the family above; the beat is 1-based, and may be fractional (2.5 is the
#                                                      second half of beat 2)
#
# A family is found when the adapter has a family with an occurrence starting within one beat of the family's first occurrence; an
# occurrence is found when the adapter has an occurrence within one beat of it of the kind written here.

meter 4 1/4
range 1 28

# the scale up from the tonic of each measure (eight notes, an eighth and then sixteenths), a sequence descending by step through the bars
family scale-up
occurrence 5 1 exact
occurrence 6 1 tonal
occurrence 7 1 tonal
occurrence 8 1 tonal

# and the scale down from the top of it (eight sixteenths)
family scale-down
occurrence 5 3 exact
occurrence 6 3 tonal
occurrence 7 3 tonal
occurrence 8 3 tonal

# the falling arpeggio D-B-G that opens measures 14 and 16
family falling-arpeggio
occurrence 14 1 exact
occurrence 16 1 exact

# the turn figure on A, G, F-sharp that opens measures 15 and 17
family turn-figure
occurrence 15 1 exact
occurrence 17 1 exact

# the five-note figure that starts on the second beat of measures 18-21: a sequence descending by step
family sequence-figure
occurrence 18 2 exact
occurrence 19 2 tonal
occurrence 20 2 tonal
occurrence 21 2 tonal

# the broken-chord figure on the last beat of measures 18-20
family broken-chord
occurrence 18 4 exact
occurrence 19 4 tonal
occurrence 20 4 tonal

# the figure of measure 26 (second beat) echoed an octave lower in measure 27
family octave-echo
occurrence 26 2 exact
occurrence 27 2 real
